subject: Physics
description: Fission, fusion, mass-energy equivalence, reactor types, Indian nuclear program

options.option_text: Two light nuclei joining into a heavier one
A heavy nucleus splitting into two lighter ones
Electrons jumping between energy levels
Atoms combining at very low temperature

questions.explanation: Fission = a heavy nucleus (e.g., U-235, Pu-239) absorbs a neutron, becomes unstable, splits into 2 lighter nuclei + 2-3 neutrons + huge energy. The released neutrons can trigger further fissions → CHAIN REACTION. Used in: atomic bombs (uncontrolled), nuclear reactors (controlled). Discovered by HAHN, STRASSMANN, MEITNER (1938). E = mc² — mass defect → energy. Distractor 1 = fusion (opposite).
questions.subject: Physics

questions.stem: NUCLEAR FUSION (the energy source of the Sun) involves:

options.option_text: Heavy nucleus splitting into smaller ones
Light nuclei combining into a heavier one
Electrons absorbing thermal radiation
Neutrons being released from atom

questions.explanation: Fusion: light nuclei (H-1, H-2 deuterium, H-3 tritium) combine → heavier nucleus (He-4) + energy. Sun uses proton-proton chain (4H → He). Requires extremely high temperature (>10⁷ K) to overcome electrostatic repulsion. Releases ~4× more energy per kg than fission. Hydrogen bomb uses fusion (triggered by fission). ITER (France, international) — major fusion reactor under construction. Indian fusion program — SST-1 + ITER participation.

questions.stem: Einstein's mass-energy equivalence E = mc² implies that:

options.option_text: Mass and energy are unrelated quantities
Small mass converts to enormous energy
Mass increases when objects move slowly
Energy is always conserved at zero mass

questions.explanation: E = mc² → c (speed of light) ≈ 3 × 10⁸ m/s; c² = 9 × 10¹⁶. So 1 kg of mass → 9 × 10¹⁶ J ≈ 25 billion kWh. In nuclear reactions, the mass of the products is slightly LESS than reactants (mass DEFECT, Δm); the missing mass is converted to energy. 1 kg uranium fission → ~8 × 10¹³ J (about same as 20,000 tons TNT). India's Pokhran tests (1974, 1998) demonstrated this principle.

questions.stem: In an Indian PHWR (Pressurised Heavy Water Reactor), 'heavy water' acts as the:

options.option_text: Fuel for the nuclear chain reaction
Moderator + coolant in reactor core
Control rod to absorb stray neutrons
Shielding from harmful radiation

questions.explanation: Heavy water (D₂O) — both moderator (slows fast neutrons to thermal speeds, increasing fission probability) AND coolant (carries heat to steam generators). PHWR uses NATURAL uranium (no enrichment needed) because D₂O moderates better than ordinary water — this is why India chose PHWR — natural uranium independence. India's 18 of 22 reactors are PHWRs (Tarapur, Kakrapar, Kaiga, Rawatbhata). Distractor 1 = uranium fuel. Distractor 3 = boron/cadmium control rods.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.stem: India's THREE-STAGE NUCLEAR PROGRAMME (designed by Homi Bhabha) aims to use which abundant fuel in the final stage?

options.option_text: Uranium-235, the standard fission fuel
Thorium-232, abundant on India's coasts
Plutonium-239, weapons-grade material
Deuterium, hydrogen heavy isotope only

questions.explanation: Bhabha's three-stage plan (1950s): STAGE 1 — PHWRs (natural U) producing Pu-239. STAGE 2 — Fast Breeder Reactors burning Pu-239, producing more Pu (and U-233 from Th-232 blanket). STAGE 3 — THORIUM-based reactors using U-233 bred from thorium. India has ~25% of world's thorium reserves (Kerala, Tamil Nadu monazite sands). PFBR (Kalpakkam) — Stage 2 reactor, criticality achieved in 2024.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.stem: The CONTROL RODS in a nuclear reactor (made of boron, cadmium) work by:

options.option_text: Speeding up the fission reaction rate
Absorbing neutrons to slow chain reaction
Reflecting neutrons back into the core
Cooling the fuel rods using water flow

questions.explanation: Control rods — made of materials with HIGH neutron-absorption cross-section: boron (B), cadmium (Cd), hafnium (Hf). Inserted DEEPER → fewer neutrons available for fission → reaction slows. Withdrawn → more neutrons → reaction speeds up. SCRAM = emergency rapid insertion of all rods. In Chernobyl disaster (1986), control rod design flaw + operator error caused runaway reaction. Distractor 1 = opposite. Distractor 4 = coolant role.

questions.stem: India's first nuclear reactor, APSARA (1956), was located at:

options.option_text: Tarapur, Maharashtra coast power site
Trombay (BARC), in Mumbai's BARC
Kalpakkam in Tamil Nadu coastline
Kakrapar in Gujarat western state

questions.explanation: APSARA — Asia's first research reactor; commissioned 4 Aug 1956 at TROMBAY (now Bhabha Atomic Research Centre, BARC), Mumbai. Designed by Homi Bhabha, used for research (not power). Other landmark Indian reactors: CIRUS (1960, Trombay; helped develop Pokhran-I device); DHRUVA (1985, BARC); KAMINI (Kalpakkam, world's only U-233 fuelled reactor). First nuclear POWER plant: TARAPUR (1969). Department of Atomic Energy (DAE) heads nuclear program.
